## Why This Is Asked
Tests a crisp bit-twiddling trick: constructing a mask anchored to the least significant set bit, plus proper zero handling.

- Mask construction via (lsb<<1) - 1
- Edge-case handling for zero input

## Why This Is Asked
Tests non-branching bit-twiddling across a 128-bit value. The triple overlap trick scales beyond 64 bits.

- Wide integer bit shifts with zero fill
- Bitwise AND to intersect bit positions

```c
unsigned hasThreeConsecutiveOnes128(uint128 x){
  uint128 t = x & (x>>1) & (x>>2);
  return t != 0;
}
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests low-level bit manipulation skills without branches, common in performance-critical code. It demonstrates proper masking, shifting, and word size preservation.

## Key Concepts
- Bit masking with 0x5555 (even positions) and 0xAAAA (odd positions)
- Left/right shifts combined with OR operation
- Branch-free operations on fixed-width integers

## Code Example
```c
uint16_t swapAdjacentBits16(uint16_t x) {
  return ((x & 0x5555) << 1) | ((x & 0xAAAA) >> 1);
}
```

## Examples
- Input: `0b10110011` (179) → Output: `0b01101101` (109)
- Input: `0b11110000` (240) → Output: `0b11110000` (240)
